at_a_glance: Phở bò is Vietnam’s best-known noodle soup: clear, fragrant beef broth, soft rice noodles, and thin slices of beef finished with herbs. It feels light, comforting, and deeply satisfying.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | sliced beef | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Herbs, lime, chili, and bean sprouts usually arrive on the side. Add them little by little so the broth stays balanced.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở bò.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of beef noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh baw
what_it_is: Phở bò is beef noodle soup with clear, fragrant broth, flat rice noodles, thin slices of beef, onion, herbs, and lime. The best bowls taste clean first, then deepen with beef sweetness and warm spice.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth first, then add herbs, lime, bean sprouts, or chili a little at a time. Keep the seasoning balanced so the broth still leads.
worth_knowing: Phở is one of Vietnam’s signature noodle soups, with northern and southern styles differing in broth sweetness, herb plates, and condiments.

at_a_glance: Phở gà is the gentler chicken version of phở, with clear broth, rice noodles, tender chicken, and fresh herbs. Order it when you want something warm, clean, and easy to love.
usually_includes: broth | rice noodles | chicken | herbs | lime
good_to_know: It is usually milder than beef phở. Add chili, lime, or herbs at the table if you want a brighter bowl.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh gah
what_it_is: Phở gà is phở with chicken, fragrant broth, flat rice noodles, onion, herbs, and lime. The bowl should taste clean first, then deepen with broth and spice.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding lime, chili, or herbs. If the bowl looks spicy, ask for less chili before it is made.
worth_knowing: Noodle soups are often breakfast or lunch food in Vietnam, but busy shops may serve them all day. The broth style can tell you as much as the toppings.

at_a_glance: Phở tái is beef phở with very thin rare beef slices that finish cooking in the hot broth. It is clean, aromatic, and more tender than the well-done beef version.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | rare beef | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: If rare beef makes you nervous, order phở chín instead. The broth should still be hot enough to soften the beef at the table.
common_options: well-done beef | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở tái.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with rare beef.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh tie
what_it_is: Phở tái is beef phở with thin rare beef slices added just before serving, so the hot broth finishes them in the bowl. It gives you tender beef without making the soup heavy.
how_to_enjoy: Let the beef sit in the broth for a moment, then taste before adding chili or lime. Choose phở chín if you want fully cooked beef from the start.
worth_knowing: Tái means rare or lightly cooked. Knowing tái versus chín helps you read many beef phở menus.

at_a_glance: Phở chín is beef phở with cooked beef slices, rice noodles, herbs, and clear fragrant broth. It is the safer choice if you want phở without rare meat.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | well-done beef | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Chín means cooked or well-done here. You still season the bowl at the table with herbs, lime, bean sprouts, or chili.
common_options: rare beef | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở chín.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with well-done beef.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh chin
what_it_is: Phở chín is beef phở with cooked beef slices, clear broth, rice noodles, onion, herbs, and lime. It keeps the classic phở flavor while avoiding rare meat.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth first, then add herbs, lime, bean sprouts, or chili little by little. The cooked beef is already ready to eat.
worth_knowing: Chín means cooked. If a menu lists tái and chín, it is asking whether you want rare beef or well-done beef.

english_translation: Pho with rare beef and brisket
at_a_glance: Phở tái nạm gives you two beef textures in one bowl: tender rare beef and richer brisket. It is still a clean broth dish, but the meat feels fuller than plain phở tái.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | rare beef | brisket | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Nạm is brisket, so this bowl has more chew and beef depth. Taste the broth before adding chili sauce or lime.
common_options: extra brisket | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở tái nạm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with rare beef and brisket.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh tie nahm
what_it_is: Phở tái nạm combines rare beef with brisket in the same bowl. The rare beef stays tender, while nạm brings a deeper beef flavor and more chew.
how_to_enjoy: Taste both beef cuts before changing the broth. Add lime or chili only after you know how rich the brisket makes the bowl.
worth_knowing: Combination phở names often list the cuts. Learning tái and nạm makes a long phở menu much easier to decode.

at_a_glance: Phở bò viên is beef phở with springy beef meatballs, clear broth, rice noodles, herbs, and lime. It is a good choice when you want texture without rare slices.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | beef meatballs | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Bò viên are bouncy beef meatballs. The texture is firmer than sliced beef and easy to recognize in a mixed phở menu.
common_options: extra meatballs | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở bò viên.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with beef meatballs.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh baw vee-en
what_it_is: Phở bò viên is phở with beef meatballs instead of sliced beef. The meatballs are springy and mild, while the broth still carries the phở aroma.
how_to_enjoy: Slice or bite the meatballs with noodles and herbs. Add chili sauce slowly so the beef broth stays clear.
worth_knowing: Bò viên appears across noodle soups and street snacks. In phở, it is the easiest beef topping for travelers who do not want rare meat.

at_a_glance: Phở đặc biệt is the special combination bowl, usually with several beef cuts such as rare beef, brisket, meatballs, tendon, or tripe depending on the shop.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | mixed beef cuts | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Đặc biệt means special, not one fixed recipe. Ask what is included if tendon, tripe, or rare beef matters.
common_options: no tripe | no tendon | extra herbs | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở đặc biệt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of special combination pho.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh dak bee-et
what_it_is: Phở đặc biệt is the house combination phở. It lets a shop show several beef textures in one bowl, from tender slices to chewier cuts.
how_to_enjoy: Taste each beef cut before adding condiments. If you are cautious, ask what meats come in the special bowl before ordering.
worth_knowing: On Vietnamese menus, đặc biệt usually means the fuller house version. It can be delicious, but it is not always the safest first order for texture-sensitive eaters.
traveler_caution: May include tendon, tripe, meatballs, brisket, and rare beef.

at_a_glance: Bún bò Huế is a bold central-Vietnam noodle soup with lemongrass, chili warmth, beef, and thick round noodles. It is richer and spicier than phở.
usually_includes: broth | rice vermicelli | beef | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Ask for less spicy if you are heat-sensitive. The broth is the point, so taste it before adding extra chili.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún bò Huế.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of spicy Hue beef noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon baw hway
what_it_is: Bún bò Huế is a bold central-Vietnam noodle soup with lemongrass, chili warmth, beef, and thicker round noodles. It is richer, deeper, and usually spicier than phở.
how_to_enjoy: Taste before adding chili. If heat is a concern, ask for less spicy early, then use the herbs and lime to brighten the broth.
worth_knowing: The name points to Huế, the former imperial capital, and the dish is strongly associated with central Vietnam. Recipes still shift by shop, especially the spice level and toppings.
traveler_caution: Ask for less spicy if heat is a concern.

at_a_glance: Bún riêu cua is crab-and-tomato vermicelli soup with a tangy red broth, soft crab mixture, tofu, herbs, and sometimes snails or pork blood cubes. It is bright, savory, and a little rustic.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | crab-tomato broth | tofu | herbs | shrimp paste optional
good_to_know: The sourness usually comes from tomato and tamarind or vinegar-like seasoning, not cream. Ask what toppings are included if you avoid shellfish or pork.
common_options: extra herbs | no shrimp paste | less chili | no pork blood
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún riêu cua.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of crab and tomato noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon ree-ew koo-ah
what_it_is: Bún riêu cua is a crab-and-tomato vermicelli soup with tangy broth, tofu, herbs, and often shrimp paste or extra pork-side toppings. It tastes brighter and more rustic than phở.
how_to_enjoy: Add herbs first, then chili or shrimp paste carefully. The broth already has sour tomato lift, so do not drown it before tasting.
worth_knowing: Riêu cua points to the crab mixture in the soup. The bowl can include shellfish, pork, tofu, and shrimp paste depending on the shop.
traveler_caution: May include shellfish, shrimp paste, pork, snails, or pork blood depending on the shop.

at_a_glance: Bún mắm is a Mekong-style noodle soup with fermented fish broth, rice vermicelli, seafood, pork, eggplant, herbs, and a deep salty aroma. It is bold on purpose.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | fermented fish broth | seafood | pork | eggplant and herbs
good_to_know: This is one of the strongest-flavored soups on a Vietnamese menu. If fermented fish sounds like too much, choose bún riêu or phở first.
common_options: extra herbs | less chili | no pork | ask what seafood
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún mắm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of fermented fish noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon mahm
what_it_is: Bún mắm is rice vermicelli in fermented fish broth with seafood, pork, eggplant, herbs, and a powerful savory aroma. It is one of the boldest soups in the menu set.
how_to_enjoy: Smell and sip before adding chili. Herbs and vegetables are not decoration; they freshen the fermented fish broth.
worth_knowing: Bún mắm is strongly associated with southern and Mekong Delta cooking. The fermented fish base is the identity, not a flaw.
regional_association: southern Vietnam and the Mekong Delta
traveler_caution: Contains fermented fish broth and often seafood or pork.

english_translation: Hanoi chicken, egg, and pork noodle soup
at_a_glance: Bún thang is a delicate Hanoi noodle soup layered with shredded chicken, egg ribbons, pork sausage, herbs, and clear broth. It is refined rather than fiery.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | clear chicken broth | shredded chicken | egg ribbons | pork sausage
good_to_know: The bowl can include pork sausage, egg, and dried-shrimp flavor. It is not just chicken soup.
common_options: extra herbs | less pepper | no pork sausage | ask about shrimp
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún thang.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of Hanoi chicken, egg, and pork noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon tang
what_it_is: Bún thang is a Hanoi soup where thin rice vermicelli sits under careful strips of chicken, egg, pork sausage, herbs, and clear broth.
how_to_enjoy: Keep the first spoonful gentle. Add chili only after tasting the broth, because the pleasure is in the layered clean flavors.
worth_knowing: Bún thang is associated with Hanoi cooking and a more delicate soup style than many southern or central bowls.
traveler_caution: May include pork, egg, and dried shrimp.

at_a_glance: Bún mọc is pork meatball noodle soup with rice vermicelli, herbs, and a clear savory broth. It is gentle, springy, and satisfying.
usually_includes: broth | rice vermicelli | pork | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Taste the broth before adding chili or lime. The side herbs are there so you can season the bowl your way.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún mọc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pork meatball noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon mawk
what_it_is: Bún mọc is rice vermicelli soup with pork meatballs, herbs, and a clear savory broth. The meatballs give the bowl its soft, springy bite.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding lime, chili, or herbs. If the bowl looks spicy, ask for less chili before it is made.
worth_knowing: Noodle soups are often breakfast or lunch food in Vietnam, but busy shops may serve them all day. The broth style can tell you as much as the toppings.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bún cá is fish noodle soup with rice vermicelli, herbs, and a light savory broth. The fish gives the bowl its clean seafood flavor.
usually_includes: broth | rice vermicelli | fish | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Noodle soups are common for breakfast or lunch, but you will find them throughout the day in busy areas.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún cá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of fish noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon kah
what_it_is: Bún cá is fish noodle soup with rice vermicelli, herbs, and light broth. The fish can be fried, steamed, or fish-cake style depending on the shop.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding lime, chili, or herbs. If the bowl looks spicy, ask for less chili before it is made.
worth_knowing: Noodle soups are often breakfast or lunch food in Vietnam, but busy shops may serve them all day. The broth style can tell you as much as the toppings.

at_a_glance: Bún ốc is snail vermicelli soup, often Hanoi-style, with a tomato-bright broth, herbs, and chewy river snails. It is tangy, clean, and more about texture than richness.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | snails | tomato broth | herbs | chili optional
good_to_know: Ốc means snails. If texture matters, ask before ordering; the snails should be chewy rather than soft like clams.
common_options: extra herbs | less chili | no shrimp paste | ask about snails
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún ốc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of snail noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon awk
what_it_is: Bún ốc is snail vermicelli soup with a tangy tomato-leaning broth, herbs, and chewy snails. It is a classic example of texture doing as much work as flavor.
how_to_enjoy: Try the snails with broth and herbs before adding extra chili. If chewy seafood textures are not your thing, choose another soup.
worth_knowing: Bún ốc is especially associated with Hanoi-style street eating, though you may see versions elsewhere.
traveler_caution: Contains snails and may include shrimp paste.

at_a_glance: Bún sứa is a coastal jellyfish noodle soup, especially familiar around Nha Trang and central beach towns. The broth is light; the jellyfish adds a crisp springy bite.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | jellyfish | light seafood broth | herbs | fish cake optional
good_to_know: Sứa means jellyfish. Order this when you want a seafood texture you probably do not see often on American menus.
common_options: extra herbs | less chili | ask what seafood | no shrimp paste
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún sứa.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of jellyfish noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon soo-uh
what_it_is: Bún sứa is a light coastal noodle soup with jellyfish, herbs, and seafood broth. The jellyfish gives a crisp springy texture rather than a strong fish flavor.
how_to_enjoy: Eat the jellyfish with herbs and broth in the same bite. Add chili slowly so the light seafood flavor stays visible.
worth_knowing: Bún sứa is especially tied to central coastal cities such as Nha Trang. For travelers, the main surprise is the texture.
traveler_caution: Contains jellyfish and seafood broth.

at_a_glance: Hủ tiếu Nam Vang is a rice-noodle soup with clear savory broth, herbs, and pork and shrimp. It usually feels lighter and more flexible than richer beef soups.
usually_includes: broth | rice noodles | pork and shrimp | herbs | lime
good_to_know: If you want a milder bowl, ask for less spicy or no chili. The soup will still have plenty of flavor.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô hủ tiếu Nam Vang.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of Phnom Penh-style rice noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh hoo tee-ew nahm vahng
what_it_is: Hủ tiếu Nam Vang is a rice-noodle soup with a clear savory broth and toppings that often include pork, shrimp, herbs, and crisp vegetables. It can feel lighter and more flexible than heavier beef soups.
how_to_enjoy: Ask whether it comes nước or khô if the shop offers both: soup-style or dry with broth on the side. Add chili slowly because the clear broth is easy to overwhelm.
worth_knowing: The name points to Nam Vang, the Vietnamese name for Phnom Penh, and the dish is especially common in southern Vietnam. Treat that as menu context rather than one fixed recipe.
regional_association: southern Vietnam and Phnom Penh-style rice-noodle shops

at_a_glance: Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is a Mekong Delta rice-noodle soup from the Mỹ Tho style, known for clear broth, chewy noodles, pork, shrimp, herbs, and fried garlic.
usually_includes: rice noodles | clear pork broth | pork | shrimp | fried garlic
good_to_know: Some shops offer it dry-style with broth on the side. Ask nước or khô if the menu gives you both options.
common_options: soup style | dry style | extra herbs | no shrimp
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of mỹ Tho-style rice noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh hoo tee-ew mee taw
what_it_is: Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is a Mekong Delta rice-noodle soup with clear broth, chewy noodles, pork, shrimp, fried garlic, and herbs. It is lighter than phở but still satisfying.
how_to_enjoy: Ask whether the shop serves it soup-style or dry-style. In dry-style, broth comes separately and the sauce coats the noodles.
worth_knowing: Mỹ Tho is a Mekong Delta city, and the name signals a southern rice-noodle style rather than a random topping.
regional_association: Mỹ Tho and the Mekong Delta
traveler_caution: Often contains pork and shrimp.

at_a_glance: Mì hoành thánh is wonton egg noodle soup with broth, egg noodles, wontons, herbs, and a bright finish from lime or chili.
usually_includes: broth | egg noodles | wontons | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Taste the broth before adding chili or lime. The side herbs are there so you can season the bowl your way.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì hoành thánh.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of wonton egg noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee hwanh tanh
what_it_is: Mì hoành thánh is wonton egg noodle soup with broth, egg noodles, wontons, herbs, and a bright finish from lime or chili. The wontons are the defining bite.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding lime, chili, or herbs. If the bowl looks spicy, ask for less chili before it is made.
worth_knowing: Noodle soups are often breakfast or lunch food in Vietnam, but busy shops may serve them all day. The broth style can tell you as much as the toppings.

at_a_glance: Mì gà is chicken egg noodle soup with egg noodles, chicken, herbs, and broth. Lime, chili, or fresh herbs can brighten the bowl.
usually_includes: broth | egg noodles | chicken | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Taste the broth before adding chili or lime. The side herbs are there so you can season the bowl your way.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken egg noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee gah
what_it_is: Mì gà is chicken egg noodle soup with broth, egg noodles, herbs, and tender chicken. It is a warmer, wheatier alternative to rice-noodle soups.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding lime, chili, or herbs. If the bowl looks spicy, ask for less chili before it is made.
worth_knowing: Noodle soups are often breakfast or lunch food in Vietnam, but busy shops may serve them all day. The broth style can tell you as much as the toppings.

at_a_glance: Miến gà is chicken glass noodle soup with clear broth, slippery glass noodles, herbs, and tender chicken. It is light but still warming.
usually_includes: broth | glass noodles | chicken | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Noodle soups are common for breakfast or lunch, but you will find them throughout the day in busy areas.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô miến gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken glass noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee-en gah
what_it_is: Miến gà is chicken glass noodle soup with clear broth, slippery glass noodles, herbs, and tender chicken. The noodles feel lighter than egg noodles.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding lime, chili, or herbs. If the bowl looks spicy, ask for less chili before it is made.
worth_knowing: Noodle soups are often breakfast or lunch food in Vietnam, but busy shops may serve them all day. The broth style can tell you as much as the toppings.

english_translation: Thick tapioca noodle soup with crab
at_a_glance: Bánh canh cua is thick tapioca-style noodle soup with crab, a glossy savory broth, herbs, and pepper. The noodles are chewy and spoonable, closer to udon texture than phở.
usually_includes: thick tapioca noodles | crab | savory broth | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: The broth can be slightly thick from the noodles. Ask about crab shell pieces if you want the easiest version to eat.
common_options: extra crab | quail egg | less pepper | ask about shells
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bánh canh cua.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of thick tapioca noodle soup with crab.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh bahn kan koo-ah
what_it_is: Bánh canh cua is crab soup with thick chewy noodles, glossy savory broth, scallions, pepper, and crab sweetness. The noodles are part of the comfort.
how_to_enjoy: Use a spoon and chopsticks together. Add pepper or chili after tasting because the crab broth can be delicate.
worth_knowing: Bánh canh noodles are much thicker than phở noodles. That chew is intentional and helps the broth feel almost stew-like.
traveler_caution: Contains crab.

english_translation: Thick noodle soup with fish cakes
at_a_glance: Bánh canh chả cá is thick noodle soup with springy fish cakes and a light seafood broth. It is gentler than crab bánh canh but still has the chewy noodle texture.
usually_includes: thick tapioca noodles | fish cakes | seafood broth | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: Chả cá means fish cake here. The fish is usually formed into slices or patties, not a whole fillet.
common_options: extra fish cake | less pepper | extra herbs | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bánh canh chả cá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of thick noodle soup with fish cakes.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh bahn kan chah kah
what_it_is: Bánh canh chả cá pairs thick chewy noodles with fish cakes and a light seafood broth. It is springy, gentle, and easier than many shellfish-heavy soups.
how_to_enjoy: Taste a fish cake with broth before adding lime or chili. The fish cake texture should be bouncy, not flaky.
worth_knowing: Chả cá can mean fish cake in many everyday menu contexts, not only the famous Hanoi turmeric fish dish.

english_translation: Thick noodle soup with pork knuckle
at_a_glance: Bánh canh giò heo is thick noodle soup with pork knuckle, scallions, pepper, and a rich pork broth. It is heavier and more collagen-rich than the seafood versions.
usually_includes: thick tapioca noodles | pork knuckle | pork broth | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: Giò heo means pork knuckle. Expect bones and skin; ask for an easier cut if that is not what you want.
common_options: extra herbs | less pepper | ask for leaner pork | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bánh canh giò heo.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of thick noodle soup with pork knuckle.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh bahn kan yaw heh-oh
what_it_is: Bánh canh giò heo is thick noodle soup with pork knuckle, pork broth, scallions, and pepper. It is rich, chewy, and more rustic than a light chicken soup.
how_to_enjoy: Expect bones, skin, and tender pork. Ask for leaner pieces if you want less collagen and easier eating.
worth_knowing: Giò heo means pork knuckle. That tells you to expect a richer texture before you order.
traveler_caution: Contains pork knuckle with bones and skin.

at_a_glance: Cháo gà is a comforting rice porridge with chicken, scallions, and gentle savory flavor. It is warm, soft, and easy when you want a simple bowl.
usually_includes: rice porridge | chicken | scallions | pepper | fried shallots
good_to_know: Many noodle soups come with herbs, lime, and bean sprouts on the side. Add a little at a time.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô cháo gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken rice porridge.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh chow gah
what_it_is: Cháo gà is a soft rice porridge with chicken, scallions, and gentle savory flavor. It is a calming bowl when you want something warm and simple.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding lime, chili, or herbs. If the bowl looks spicy, ask for less chili before it is made.
worth_knowing: Noodle soups are often breakfast or lunch food in Vietnam, but busy shops may serve them all day. The broth style can tell you as much as the toppings.

worth_knowing: Travelers often meet this dish around Đà Lạt, though the herb and style also connect to Phú Yên.

at_a_glance: Chè ba màu is the classic three-color dessert cup: beans, pandan jelly, coconut milk, and crushed ice layered so every spoonful changes texture.
usually_includes: mung beans | red beans | pandan jelly | coconut milk | crushed ice
good_to_know: This is as much about texture as sweetness. Stir lightly if you want the coconut milk to reach every layer.
common_options: less sweet | less ice | extra coconut milk | takeaway cup
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly chè ba màu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of three-color dessert.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee cheh bah mow
what_it_is: Chè ba màu means three-color chè, usually a layered cup of beans, jellies, coconut milk, and ice.
how_to_enjoy: Dig down through the layers before stirring everything together. The contrast between creamy, chewy, icy, and soft is the point.
worth_knowing: Chè is Vietnam’s broad dessert-drink world, and ba màu is one of the easiest first cups for Americans to understand visually.

at_a_glance: Chè đậu xanh is mung bean sweet soup or pudding, often soft, lightly sweet, and rounded with coconut milk. It is simple comfort rather than a flashy dessert.
usually_includes: mung beans | sugar | coconut milk optional | ice optional
good_to_know: Đậu xanh means mung bean. Ask for less coconut if you want the bean flavor cleaner.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô chè đậu xanh.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of mung bean sweet soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh cheh dow sanh
what_it_is: Chè đậu xanh is a mung bean chè, served warm, chilled, or over ice depending on the shop.
how_to_enjoy: Stir if coconut milk is added, then taste before asking for more sweetness or ice.
worth_knowing: Mung bean sweets are common across Vietnam because they are filling, gentle, and easy to pair with coconut.

at_a_glance: Chè đậu đỏ is red bean sweet soup, usually soft beans in syrup with coconut milk or ice. It is earthy, sweet, and filling.
usually_includes: red beans | sugar syrup | coconut milk optional | ice optional
good_to_know: The beans should be tender but still recognizable. Ask for less sweet if you want it lighter.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô chè đậu đỏ.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of red bean sweet soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh cheh dow daw
what_it_is: Chè đậu đỏ is red bean chè, a bean-based dessert that can be served warm or cold.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it slowly like a small bowl, not a drink. Coconut milk makes it richer.
worth_knowing: Bean-based chè may surprise Americans because beans move from savory territory into dessert.

at_a_glance: Chè đậu đen is black bean sweet soup, often served with syrup, coconut milk, and ice. It tastes deeper and earthier than red bean chè.
usually_includes: black beans | sugar syrup | coconut milk optional | ice
good_to_know: It is a cooling dessert on hot days. The beans give it more chew and body than a simple pudding.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô chè đậu đen.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of black bean sweet soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh cheh dow den
what_it_is: Chè đậu đen is black bean chè, a sweet bean dessert that is usually spooned cold or over ice.
how_to_enjoy: Stir in coconut milk if served, then spoon beans and syrup together.
worth_knowing: Black bean chè is a classic example of Vietnamese sweets caring about texture and refreshment as much as sugar.

at_a_glance: Chè bắp is sweet corn pudding, usually made with tender corn, sticky rice or tapioca body, coconut milk, and gentle sweetness.
usually_includes: sweet corn | coconut milk | tapioca or sticky rice | sugar
good_to_know: Bắp means corn. Expect a soft spoon dessert, not a corn drink.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly chè bắp.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of sweet corn pudding.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee cheh bap
what_it_is: Chè bắp is corn chè, a creamy-sweet bowl where corn flavor stays visible.
how_to_enjoy: Eat warm or chilled depending on the shop. Coconut milk and a little salt can make the corn taste sweeter.
worth_knowing: Corn shows up in Vietnamese desserts more naturally than many Americans expect.

at_a_glance: Chè chuối is banana coconut pudding with soft banana, coconut milk, tapioca pearls, and often peanuts or sesame on top.
usually_includes: banana | coconut milk | tapioca pearls | peanuts optional | sesame
good_to_know: The banana is usually cooked until soft and fragrant. Ask no peanuts if needed.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly chè chuối.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of banana coconut pudding.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee cheh choo-ee
what_it_is: Chè chuối is a banana-and-coconut chè, creamy and spoonable rather than icy.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm or chilled and get banana, coconut, and tapioca in the same spoonful.
worth_knowing: This is a friendly first chè for travelers because banana and coconut feel familiar while the texture is Vietnamese.
traveler_caution: Often contains peanuts.

at_a_glance: Chè Thái is a fruit-and-jelly dessert with coconut milk, often durian, jackfruit, longan, lychee, and colorful jellies. It is creamy, fragrant, and loud in a good way.
usually_includes: coconut milk | fruit | jellies | durian optional | crushed ice
good_to_know: Ask about durian if the aroma worries you. Some cups include it by default; others keep it optional.
common_options: no durian | less sweet | less ice | extra fruit
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly chè thái.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of Thai-style fruit dessert.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee cheh tie
what_it_is: Chè Thái is a rich fruit chè inspired by Thai-style dessert flavors, with coconut milk and mixed tropical fruit or jellies.
how_to_enjoy: Stir enough to chill the coconut milk, then take small spoonfuls so the fruit and jelly textures stay distinct.
worth_knowing: This is one of the more dessert-like chè cups: creamy, fruity, icy, and sometimes durian-forward.
traveler_caution: May contain durian and dairy-style additions depending on the shop.

at_a_glance: Chè khúc bạch is a chilled dessert with soft milk-jelly cubes, lychee or longan, syrup, and sliced almonds. It is lighter and cleaner than coconut-heavy chè.
usually_includes: milk jelly | lychee or longan | clear syrup | almonds | ice
good_to_know: The cubes should be silky and lightly creamy, not chewy like tapioca. It is a good choice when you want a cooler, gentler dessert.
common_options: less sweet | extra lychee | no almonds | less ice
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly chè khúc bạch.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of almond panna cotta dessert.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee cheh khook bak
what_it_is: Chè khúc bạch is a modern chilled chè with creamy jelly cubes, fruit, syrup, and almonds.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it cold and keep the syrup light. The best bites pair a jelly cube with lychee or longan.
worth_knowing: Compared with bean-based chè, khúc bạch feels closer to panna cotta in syrup, which makes it approachable as a first chilled chè.
traveler_caution: Usually contains dairy and almonds.

english_translation: Sticky rice balls in ginger syrup
at_a_glance: Chè trôi nước is warm glutinous rice balls filled with mung bean and served in ginger syrup, often with coconut milk and sesame.
usually_includes: glutinous rice balls | mung bean filling | ginger syrup | coconut milk optional | sesame
good_to_know: This is a warm dessert, not an iced cup. The ginger syrup is part of the comfort.
common_options: extra ginger | less sweet | coconut milk | takeaway bowl
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly chè trôi nước.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of sticky rice balls in ginger syrup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee cheh choy nook
what_it_is: Chè trôi nước is a warm Vietnamese sweet of chewy rice balls in ginger syrup, with a soft mung-bean center.
how_to_enjoy: Cut or bite carefully; the rice balls are chewy and can be hot inside. Spoon ginger syrup with each bite.
worth_knowing: The dessert is tied to family and festival-style sweets, so it feels more ceremonial than a quick iced chè.

english_translation: Jelly and faux pomegranate seed dessert
at_a_glance: Chè sương sa hạt lựu is a jelly dessert with agar, coconut milk, and faux pomegranate-seed cubes that pop with chewy texture.
usually_includes: agar jelly | faux pomegranate seeds | coconut milk | ice | syrup
good_to_know: Hạt lựu means pomegranate seeds, but these are usually colorful starch jellies, not real pomegranate.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly chè sương sa hạt lựu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of jelly and faux pomegranate seed dessert.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee cheh soong sah hat loo-oo
what_it_is: Chè sương sa hạt lựu is a chilled jelly-and-coconut dessert where color and chew do most of the work.
how_to_enjoy: Stir lightly and scoop across the jellies so you get more than one texture at once.
worth_knowing: This is a texture-first dessert, a good reminder that Vietnamese sweets often prize chew and coolness.

at_a_glance: Tàu hũ nước đường is soft tofu pudding in ginger sugar syrup. It is silky, warm or chilled, and gentler than many coconut-heavy desserts.
usually_includes: soft tofu pudding | ginger syrup | sugar syrup | coconut optional
good_to_know: This is dessert tofu, not savory tofu. The texture should be very soft and spoonable.
common_options: warm | cold | extra ginger | less sweet
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần tàu hũ nước đường.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of silken tofu with ginger syrup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn tow hoo nook duhng
what_it_is: Tàu hũ nước đường is silken tofu pudding served with sweet ginger syrup.
how_to_enjoy: Spoon carefully so the tofu stays silky. Ginger syrup gives the dessert its warmth.
worth_knowing: It is a useful gentle dessert when you want something sweet but not icy, fried, or heavy.

at_a_glance: Sương sáo is grass jelly, a dark herbal jelly served with syrup, ice, or milk. It is cooling, lightly bitter, and very soft.
usually_includes: grass jelly | syrup | ice | milk optional
good_to_know: The flavor is herbal rather than fruity. Choose it when you want something cooling and not too rich.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần sương sáo.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grass jelly.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn soong sow
what_it_is: Sương sáo is grass jelly, usually cut into cubes or strips and served as a light dessert or drink topping.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it cold with syrup or milk. The soft jelly texture is the main event.
worth_knowing: Grass jelly sits between drink and dessert in Vietnam, especially on hot days.

at_a_glance: Bánh flan is Vietnamese caramel flan, usually silky custard with dark caramel and sometimes crushed ice or coffee.
usually_includes: egg custard | caramel | crushed ice optional | coffee optional
good_to_know: Some shops serve flan with coffee poured over ice. Ask if you want it plain.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh flan.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of caramel flan.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn flan
what_it_is: Bánh flan is caramel custard adopted into Vietnam’s dessert-counter culture.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it cold and spoon caramel with each bite. Coffee makes it more bitter and grown-up.
worth_knowing: This is one of the most familiar desserts for Americans, but Vietnamese shops often serve it colder and more casual.

at_a_glance: Rau câu dừa is coconut jelly, often layered with clear coconut water jelly and creamy coconut milk jelly.
usually_includes: coconut jelly | coconut water | coconut milk | agar
good_to_know: Rau câu means agar jelly. It should be clean, cool, and sliceable.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần rau câu dừa.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of coconut jelly.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn row cow yoo-uh
what_it_is: Rau câu dừa is a coconut agar dessert with a firm, refreshing jelly texture.
how_to_enjoy: Eat cold in small pieces. It is lighter than ice cream and cleaner than coconut pudding.
worth_knowing: Agar jellies are common in Vietnamese sweets because they hold shape and stay refreshing in heat.

at_a_glance: Kem dừa is coconut ice cream, often served in a coconut shell or cup with coconut flakes, peanuts, or jelly toppings.
usually_includes: coconut ice cream | coconut flakes | peanuts optional | jelly optional
good_to_know: Ask no peanuts if needed. The best versions taste like coconut, not just vanilla with coconut bits.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly kem dừa.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of coconut ice cream.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kem yoo-uh
what_it_is: Kem dừa is a coconut ice-cream dessert, usually more tropical and textural than a plain scoop.
how_to_enjoy: Eat before it melts and mix in toppings slowly so the coconut flavor stays clear.
worth_knowing: Coconut desserts are a strong through-line in Vietnamese sweets, from chè to ice cream.
traveler_caution: Often contains dairy and peanuts.

english_translation: Layered pandan and mung bean cake
at_a_glance: Bánh da lợn is a layered steamed cake, usually pandan-green and mung-bean-yellow, with a chewy tapioca-rice texture and gentle coconut sweetness.
usually_includes: tapioca-rice batter | pandan | mung bean | coconut milk | steamed layers
good_to_know: The name means pig-skin cake because of the layered texture, not because it contains pork.
common_options: takeaway | share pieces | less sweet | ask about coconut
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh da lợn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of layered pandan and mung bean cake.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn zah luhn
what_it_is: Bánh da lợn is a chewy layered steamed cake made with pandan, mung bean, coconut milk, and starches.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it in small pieces and notice the chew. It is more springy than fluffy.
worth_knowing: For Americans, the useful cue is texture: this is a soft, chewy steamed sweet, not a baked cake.
traveler_caution: Usually contains coconut milk.

at_a_glance: Bánh chuối nướng is baked banana cake, often dense, coconut-rich, and caramelized at the edges.
usually_includes: banana | coconut milk | bread or starch base | sugar
good_to_know: This is not fluffy American banana bread. Expect a moist, custardy texture.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh chuối nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of baked banana cake.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn choo-ee noong
what_it_is: Bánh chuối nướng is a baked banana dessert where ripe banana and coconut create a dense slice.
how_to_enjoy: Eat at room temperature or slightly warm. It pairs well with tea or coffee.
worth_knowing: Vietnamese banana sweets often lean soft, sticky, and coconut-rich rather than cake-like.

at_a_glance: Bánh bò is honeycomb cake, a chewy steamed or baked rice cake with airy tunnels and gentle coconut sweetness.
usually_includes: rice flour | tapioca starch | coconut milk | yeast or leavening
good_to_know: The honeycomb texture is the point. It should bounce a little when you bite it.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh bò.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of honeycomb cake.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn baw
what_it_is: Bánh bò is a Vietnamese honeycomb cake, usually chewy and lightly sweet rather than fluffy.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it as a snack cake. Notice the springy texture more than frosting or richness.
worth_knowing: For Americans, bánh bò is useful as a texture lesson: cake can mean chewy, steamed, and coconut-scented.

at_a_glance: Bánh cam is a fried sesame ball with a crisp chewy shell and sweet mung bean filling. It is snacky, round, and best fresh.
usually_includes: glutinous rice shell | mung bean filling | sesame | fried crust
good_to_know: The outside should be crisp-chewy while the filling stays soft. Freshness matters.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh cam.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of sesame ball.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn kahm
what_it_is: Bánh cam is a Vietnamese sesame ball, a fried glutinous rice pastry with sweet filling.
how_to_enjoy: Eat while the shell still has crunch. It is richer than it looks.
worth_knowing: This is a familiar shape across Chinese-Vietnamese and Southeast Asian snack worlds, but local fillings and texture vary.

at_a_glance: Bánh pía is a flaky southern pastry, often from Sóc Trăng, filled with mung bean, salted egg yolk, and sometimes durian.
usually_includes: flaky pastry | mung bean filling | salted egg yolk | durian optional
good_to_know: Ask about durian before buying if the aroma is a concern. The pastry can be rich and sweet-salty.
common_options: no durian | boxed gift | single pastry | share pieces
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh pía.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of durian mung bean pastry.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn pee-ah
what_it_is: Bánh pía is a layered pastry with a dense sweet filling, commonly mung bean plus salted egg yolk and sometimes durian.
how_to_enjoy: Cut it into small wedges. It is richer than it looks and works well with tea.
worth_knowing: Bánh pía is strongly associated with Sóc Trăng and southern gift/snack culture.
traveler_caution: May contain durian and salted egg yolk.

at_a_glance: Chuối nếp nướng is grilled banana wrapped in sticky rice, usually served with coconut sauce, peanuts, and sesame. It is smoky, chewy, and sweet.
usually_includes: banana | sticky rice | coconut sauce | peanuts | sesame
good_to_know: The grilled wrapper gives a toasty edge while the coconut sauce makes it dessert-rich.
common_options: extra coconut sauce | no peanuts | share pieces | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần chuối nếp nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grilled banana with sticky rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn choo-ee nep noong
what_it_is: Chuối nếp nướng is banana wrapped in sticky rice, grilled, then topped with coconut sauce and crunch.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm if possible, while the sticky rice still has a grilled edge.
worth_knowing: This is a street sweet where smoke, coconut, banana, and chewy rice all matter.
traveler_caution: Often contains peanuts.

at_a_glance: Bánh cốm is green young-rice cake, usually sticky and fragrant with mung bean filling. It is closely tied to Hanoi gift culture.
usually_includes: young green rice | mung bean filling | sugar | pandan-like aroma
good_to_know: Cốm means young green rice flakes. The texture is sticky and chewy, not fluffy cake.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh cốm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of green rice flakes cake.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn kohm
what_it_is: Bánh cốm is a sweet green rice cake with mung bean inside.
how_to_enjoy: Eat in small pieces with tea. The rice fragrance is subtle, so do not expect a loud dessert.
worth_knowing: Bánh cốm is especially associated with Hanoi, where cốm is a seasonal and gift-worthy flavor.

at_a_glance: Bánh phu thê is a translucent chewy cake with mung bean and coconut, often wrapped for weddings or gifts.
usually_includes: tapioca-like wrapper | mung bean | coconut | sugar
good_to_know: The name means husband-and-wife cake. It is symbolic as much as snackable.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh phu thê.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of husband-and-wife cake.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn foo tay
what_it_is: Bánh phu thê is a chewy sweet cake with a mung bean center, often connected to wedding customs.
how_to_enjoy: Unwrap and eat in small bites. The texture is sticky and translucent, not bread-like.
worth_knowing: This is a dessert with cultural meaning; the name points to marriage and pairing.

at_a_glance: Sữa chua nếp cẩm is yogurt with fermented black sticky rice. It is tangy, creamy, gently boozy-smelling, and chewy from the rice.
usually_includes: yogurt | black sticky rice | fermented rice syrup | ice optional
good_to_know: The black sticky rice brings a fermented aroma and chew. It is dessert, not just a yogurt cup.
common_options: less sweet | more sticky rice | less ice | takeaway cup
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly sữa chua nếp cẩm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of yogurt with black sticky rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee soo-uh choo-ah nep kahm
what_it_is: Sữa chua nếp cẩm combines tart yogurt with sweet fermented black sticky rice.
how_to_enjoy: Stir lightly so the yogurt and rice meet without losing all the chewy rice pockets.
worth_knowing: This is a good example of Vietnamese desserts using fermentation and texture, not only sugar.
traveler_caution: Contains dairy.

at_a_glance: Trái cây dĩa is a mixed fruit plate, usually fresh cut fruit served cold with salt-chili dip, yogurt, or syrup depending on the shop.
usually_includes: fresh fruit | ice optional | salt-chili dip optional | yogurt optional
good_to_know: Dĩa means plate. Ask what fruit is included if you are avoiding durian, jackfruit, or anything very ripe.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no coconut | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần trái cây dĩa.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of mixed fruit plate.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn chai kay yee-ah
what_it_is: Trái cây dĩa is a plate of cut fruit, a simple cooling dessert or snack.
how_to_enjoy: Use salt-chili dip lightly if it comes with the fruit. It can make mango, guava, or pineapple pop.
worth_knowing: Fresh fruit is an everyday Vietnam dessert move, especially when you want something lighter than chè.

at_a_glance: Kem bơ is avocado ice cream or avocado cream, famously associated with Đà Lạt-style dessert shops. It is creamy, green, and richer than a fruit smoothie.
usually_includes: avocado | ice cream | condensed milk | coconut optional
good_to_know: Bơ means avocado here, not butter. Expect dessert creaminess rather than a savory avocado flavor.
common_options: less sweet | extra ice cream | no coconut | takeaway cup
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly kem bơ.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of avocado ice cream.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kem buh
what_it_is: Kem bơ is a cold avocado dessert, often blended avocado topped with ice cream or coconut.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it while cold and stir just enough to mix the avocado with the ice cream.
worth_knowing: Đà Lạt is especially known for avocado desserts, and kem bơ is the easy order to remember.
traveler_caution: Usually contains dairy.

at_a_glance: Cà phê sữa đá is Vietnam’s iconic iced milk coffee: strong phin-brewed robusta, sweetened condensed milk, and plenty of ice. Bold, creamy, and made for hot afternoons.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | condensed milk | ice
good_to_know: It is usually stronger and sweeter than it looks. Ask for less sweet or more ice if you want it lighter.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê sữa đá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of Vietnamese iced milk coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay soo-uh dah
what_it_is: Cà phê sữa đá is strong Vietnamese robusta coffee mixed with sweetened condensed milk and poured over ice. It is bold, creamy, and made for hot afternoons.
how_to_enjoy: Stir well before drinking so the condensed milk lifts through the coffee. Ask for less sweet or more ice if you want it lighter.
worth_knowing: This is the everyday icon of Vietnamese iced coffee. The flavor comes from robusta strength, condensed milk sweetness, and a slow phin drip.

at_a_glance: Cà phê đen đá is strong phin-brewed black coffee poured over ice. It is bold, bitter, and refreshing when you want the Vietnamese coffee hit without condensed milk.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | ice
good_to_know: This is the unsweetened or lightly sweetened black-coffee lane. Ask for đường riêng if you want sugar on the side.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê đen đá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of Vietnamese iced black coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay den dah
what_it_is: Cà phê đen đá is iced black Vietnamese coffee. Without condensed milk, the robusta comes through darker, sharper, and more refreshing over ice.
how_to_enjoy: Sip before adding sugar. If it is stronger than expected, ask for more ice or sugar on the side instead of turning it into milk coffee.
worth_knowing: This is the cleanest way to taste the coffee base behind many Vietnamese café drinks: phin-brewed, bold, and often more intense than a typical American iced coffee.

at_a_glance: Cà phê sữa nóng is hot Vietnamese milk coffee: phin-brewed robusta softened with condensed milk. It is sweet, strong, and better when you want the café ritual without ice.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | condensed milk
good_to_know: The condensed milk settles low in the cup. Stir until the color evens out, then decide whether you want it stronger next time.
common_options: less sweet | stronger | with ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê sữa nóng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of hot Vietnamese milk coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay soo-uh nawng
what_it_is: Cà phê sữa nóng is hot phin coffee with condensed milk. It keeps the sweet, creamy Vietnamese coffee profile but drops the ice.
how_to_enjoy: Stir from the bottom so the condensed milk fully blends into the coffee. Drink it slowly while the cup is still warm.
worth_knowing: Hot milk coffee is useful in rainy weather, air-conditioned cafés, or early mornings when iced coffee feels too sharp.

at_a_glance: Cà phê đen nóng is hot black Vietnamese coffee from a phin filter. It is sharper, more aromatic, and more intense than the milk versions.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter
good_to_know: Order this when you want the robusta flavor to lead. Ask for sugar on the side if you do not want it pre-sweetened.
common_options: sugar on the side | stronger | with ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê đen nóng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of hot black coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay den nawng
what_it_is: Cà phê đen nóng is hot black Vietnamese coffee, usually phin-brewed and served small, strong, and aromatic.
how_to_enjoy: Treat it like a slow strong cup, not a large mug. Ask for sugar separately if you want to control the sweetness.
worth_knowing: This order is a good bridge between espresso habits and Vietnamese phin culture: concentrated like a short coffee, but brewed with a different rhythm.

at_a_glance: Bạc xỉu is a softer, milkier coffee with more sweet milk than coffee. It is creamy, gentle, and a good pick if regular Vietnamese coffee feels too strong.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | condensed milk | fresh milk | ice optional
good_to_know: Think of it as coffee-flavored milk rather than a heavy caffeine hit. It is often served iced.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | less coffee | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly bạc xỉu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of light milk coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee bak see-ew
what_it_is: Bạc xỉu is a milkier, gentler coffee drink with more sweet milk than coffee. It is creamy and friendly if regular Vietnamese coffee feels too strong.
how_to_enjoy: Order it iced when you want something cool and soft. Think of it as coffee-flavored milk rather than a heavy caffeine hit.
worth_knowing: Bạc xỉu is closely associated with Saigon and Chợ Lớn café culture. The idea is simple and charming: lots of milk, just enough coffee.

at_a_glance: Cà phê trứng is Hanoi’s famous egg coffee: strong coffee under a whipped egg-yolk cream that drinks like warm tiramisu. It is rich, sweet, and worth trying slowly.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | egg cream | condensed milk
good_to_know: The egg is whipped into a custardy foam, not cooked like breakfast eggs. Ask whether it is served hot or iced before ordering.
common_options: hot | iced | less sweet | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê trứng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of egg coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay choong
what_it_is: Cà phê trứng is Hanoi-born egg coffee: strong coffee topped with whipped egg-yolk cream, sugar, and condensed milk. It tastes more like a warm coffee custard than a normal cup.
how_to_enjoy: Try the foam first, then stir if you want the creamy layer to blend into the coffee. Order it when you want a small dessert-like café moment.
worth_knowing: Egg coffee is one of Vietnam’s most famous coffee creations and is strongly tied to Hanoi café culture. The backstory often points to resourceful cafés making richness from scarce milk.

at_a_glance: Cà phê cốt dừa is coconut coffee, often served cold with creamy coconut blended or layered against strong coffee. It feels tropical, rich, and almost dessert-like.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | coconut cream | ice
good_to_know: This can be closer to a café treat than a plain coffee. Ask for less sweet if you want the coffee bitterness to stay visible.
common_options: less sweet | more coffee | less ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê cốt dừa.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of coconut coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay koht yoo-uh
what_it_is: Cà phê cốt dừa is coconut coffee, usually cold, creamy, and layered or blended so coconut sweetness meets strong Vietnamese coffee.
how_to_enjoy: Let it soften for a moment if it arrives icy or blended. Stir lightly when you want the coconut and coffee to mix instead of staying in layers.
worth_knowing: Coconut coffee shows the modern playful side of Vietnamese cafés: still built on a bold coffee base, but closer to a tropical dessert drink.

at_a_glance: Cà phê muối is salt coffee, a creamy Vietnamese coffee with a lightly salted foam that makes the bitter robusta taste rounder and more caramel-like.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | salted cream | condensed milk
good_to_know: The salt should balance the sweetness, not taste like seawater. It is strongly associated with Huế-style café creativity.
common_options: less sweet | more coffee | iced | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê muối.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of salt coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay moo-ee
what_it_is: Cà phê muối is salt coffee: robusta coffee with sweet milk and a lightly salted cream. The salt makes the cup taste round, rich, and caramel-like.
how_to_enjoy: Sip before judging the salt. A good cup should feel balanced, with the salt sharpening the cream and softening the coffee bitterness.
worth_knowing: Salt coffee is especially associated with Huế, and it has spread because the sweet-salty balance feels both familiar and surprising.

at_a_glance: Cà phê phin is Vietnamese drip coffee brewed through the small metal filter sitting on the cup. Order it when you want the slow, classic coffee ritual itself.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter
good_to_know: Phin coffee takes a few minutes. The pause is normal: the drip, the glass, and the slow first sip are part of Vietnamese café culture.
common_options: black | with condensed milk | iced | hot
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê phin.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of Vietnamese drip coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay fin
what_it_is: Cà phê phin is coffee brewed through Vietnam’s small metal drip filter. It is less a flavor name than a way of making and waiting for the cup.
how_to_enjoy: Give the drip time. When the filter finishes, stir if milk is present, add ice if you want it cold, and taste before changing sweetness.
worth_knowing: The phin filter is part of the social rhythm of Vietnamese cafés: order, sit, watch the drip, then linger over a strong small glass.

at_a_glance: Cà phê sữa tươi is coffee with fresh milk instead of only condensed milk. It is still Vietnamese coffee, but smoother, lighter, and less sticky-sweet.
usually_includes: robusta coffee | phin filter | fresh milk | ice optional
good_to_know: This is a useful middle lane if condensed milk feels too heavy but black coffee feels too sharp.
common_options: less sweet | more coffee | iced | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê sữa tươi.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of coffee with fresh milk.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay soo-uh too-ee
what_it_is: Cà phê sữa tươi is Vietnamese coffee with fresh milk. Compared with condensed-milk coffee, it usually tastes lighter, smoother, and less syrupy.
how_to_enjoy: Choose it when you want milk coffee without the full sweetness of condensed milk. Ask for less sugar if the café sweetens it separately.
worth_knowing: Fresh-milk coffee is common in modern cafés, where Vietnamese coffee habits meet latte-style preferences.

at_a_glance: Cà phê đá xay is blended iced coffee, a cold café drink where coffee, ice, milk, or cream become a thick shake-like cup.
usually_includes: coffee | ice | milk or cream | sugar optional
good_to_know: Expect a dessert texture more than a sidewalk phin coffee. Ask for less sugar if you want it less sweet.
common_options: less sugar | more coffee | no whipped cream | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê đá xay.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of blended iced coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay dah sai
what_it_is: Cà phê đá xay is blended iced coffee, usually coffee, ice, milk or cream, and sugar turned into a thick café drink.
how_to_enjoy: Treat it like a cold dessert coffee. Ask for less sugar or more coffee if you want the drink less sweet and more grown-up.
worth_knowing: This is the menu item for modern air-conditioned cafés, not the sidewalk phin ritual. It is still useful when you want a cold familiar order.

at_a_glance: Cà phê latte is the familiar milk-forward latte found in modern Vietnamese cafés. It is useful when you want a softer coffee order in an international café setting.
usually_includes: espresso-style coffee | steamed or fresh milk
good_to_know: This is not the classic phin drink, but many city cafés offer it beside Vietnamese coffee styles.
common_options: hot | iced | less sweet | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê latte.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of latte.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay lah-tay
what_it_is: Cà phê latte is a latte-style coffee order with milk. It is the safer familiar choice in cafés that also serve espresso drinks.
how_to_enjoy: Ask whether it is hot or iced if the menu does not say. If you want a Vietnamese-style cup, choose phin coffee instead.
worth_knowing: Vietnam’s café scene now includes both traditional phin drinks and global espresso drinks, so latte can be useful even though it is not the local classic.

at_a_glance: Cà phê espresso is a short, concentrated coffee order in modern cafés. It is quick, strong, and different from the slower phin style.
usually_includes: espresso coffee | small cup
good_to_know: Use this word in espresso-machine cafés. At traditional coffee shops, a black phin coffee may be the more natural strong order.
common_options: single | double | hot | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê espresso.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of espresso.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay ess-press-oh
what_it_is: Cà phê espresso is espresso, a short concentrated coffee from an espresso machine rather than a phin filter.
how_to_enjoy: Use this in modern cafés where espresso machines are visible. In a traditional shop, ask for black phin coffee instead.
worth_knowing: Espresso belongs to Vietnam’s modern café layer, but it is not the same experience as watching coffee drip through a phin.

at_a_glance: Cà phê mocha is coffee with chocolate and milk, a modern café drink for when you want coffee but also something sweet and dessert-like.
usually_includes: coffee | milk | chocolate
good_to_know: It is familiar and easy in bigger cafés, but it will not tell you as much about Vietnam’s phin coffee culture as the local styles do.
common_options: hot | iced | less sweet | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê mocha.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of mocha coffee.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee kah fay moh-kah
what_it_is: Cà phê mocha is coffee with milk and chocolate. It is sweet, soft, and familiar when you want dessert energy more than a classic Vietnamese coffee.
how_to_enjoy: Ask for less sweet if you want the coffee to show through. It can be hot or iced depending on the café.
worth_knowing: Mocha belongs to Vietnam’s modern café menu layer. The cultural story is stronger in phin, egg, salt, coconut, and bạc xỉu drinks.

at_a_glance: Trà đá is plain iced tea, often served automatically at casual restaurants and street-food spots. It is light, unsweetened or barely sweet, and good with rich food.
usually_includes: tea | ice
good_to_know: It may come free or very cheap, depending on the place. Bottled tea is a different order.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly trà đá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of iced tea.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee chah dah
what_it_is: Trà đá is an iced tea. Depending on the style, it can be plain and light or sweet enough to feel like a dessert drink.
how_to_enjoy: Ask for less sweet before it is mixed. Plain tea is light with meals; milk tea and fruit tea can be dessert-like.
worth_knowing: Tea ranges from plain meal tea to sweet fruit or milk tea. The same English word can cover very different drinks.

at_a_glance: Trà nóng is a simple hot tea order, usually served in a cup or small pot. It is light, calming, and good beside a meal.
usually_includes: tea
good_to_know: Iced tea may come very cold and light. Hot tea is usually served in a cup or small pot.
common_options: less sweet | honey | hot | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly trà nóng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of hot tea.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee chah nawng
what_it_is: Trà nóng is a hot tea. Depending on the style, it can be plain and light or sweet enough to feel like a dessert drink.
how_to_enjoy: Ask for less sweet before it is mixed. Plain tea is light with meals; milk tea and fruit tea can be dessert-like.
worth_knowing: Tea ranges from plain meal tea to sweet fruit or milk tea. The same English word can cover very different drinks.

at_a_glance: Trà xanh is green tea, usually light, grassy, and served hot or iced depending on the place.
usually_includes: green tea | hot water or ice | sugar optional
good_to_know: If you want unsweetened tea, ask before ordering bottled or café versions.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly trà xanh.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of green tea.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee chah sanh
what_it_is: Trà xanh is green tea, one of the simplest non-coffee drinks to recognize.
how_to_enjoy: Drink it plain with food or iced on a hot day. Sugar changes the drink quickly.
worth_knowing: Tea can mean plain meal tea or a sweet café drink, so xanh helps anchor this as green tea.

at_a_glance: Trà sen is lotus tea, a fragrant tea with a soft floral aroma rather than fruit sweetness.
usually_includes: tea | lotus scent | hot water or ice | sugar optional
good_to_know: Sen means lotus. Choose it for aroma, not for a sugary drink.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly trà sen.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of lotus tea.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee chah sen
what_it_is: Trà sen is tea scented with lotus, a classic Vietnamese flavor cue.
how_to_enjoy: Try it lightly sweet or plain so the lotus aroma stays clear.
worth_knowing: Lotus is culturally important in Vietnam, and lotus tea is one of the gentler ways to taste that association.

at_a_glance: Trà lài is jasmine tea, floral and lighter than milk tea or fruit tea.
usually_includes: jasmine tea | hot water or ice | sugar optional
good_to_know: Lài means jasmine. It should smell floral without tasting like perfume.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly trà lài.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of jasmine tea.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee chah lie
what_it_is: Trà lài is jasmine-scented tea, served hot or cold.
how_to_enjoy: Drink plain with food or lightly sweetened as a café tea.
worth_knowing: Jasmine tea is an easy bridge for travelers who want something aromatic but not creamy.

at_a_glance: Trà gừng is ginger tea, warm, spicy, and soothing rather than dessert-like.
usually_includes: ginger | tea or hot water | sugar or honey optional
good_to_know: Gừng means ginger. It can feel sharp if the ginger is strong.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly trà gừng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of ginger tea.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee chah goong
what_it_is: Trà gừng is ginger tea, often ordered hot for comfort.
how_to_enjoy: Sip hot and ask less sweet if you want the ginger bite to stay clear.
worth_knowing: Ginger drinks are part comfort, part home-remedy habit in Vietnam.

at_a_glance: Trà tắc is kumquat iced tea, bright, sweet-tart, and especially good with salty snacks.
usually_includes: tea | kumquat | ice | sugar
good_to_know: Tắc is kumquat. It tastes sharper and more aromatic than ordinary lemon tea.
common_options: less sweet | more ice | no ice | takeaway
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly trà tắc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of kumquat iced tea.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee chah tak
what_it_is: Trà tắc is iced tea mixed with kumquat juice.
how_to_enjoy: Stir before drinking and ask less sugar if you want more tartness.
worth_knowing: Kumquat shows up across Vietnamese drinks because it gives citrus brightness without tasting exactly like lime.

at_a_glance: Trà chanh is lemon or lime tea, a bright iced tea often served sweet and cold.
usually_includes: tea | lemon or lime | ice | sugar
good_to_know: It is usually sweeter than plain tea. Ask less sweet before it is mixed.

quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht chai bee-ah tie-ger
what_it_is: Bia Tiger is a tiger beer, usually served cold and paired with snacks or a shared table meal.
how_to_enjoy: Ask whether it comes by glass, can, bottle, or draft. Many casual places serve beer with ice.
worth_knowing: Simple drinks still have local habits: beer may come with ice, bottled water may not be chilled, and canned drinks may arrive with a glass.

at_a_glance: Rượu đế is strong Vietnamese rice liquor, usually clear and poured in small shots. It is not a casual soft drink.
usually_includes: rice liquor | small glass | shared bottle
good_to_know: Rượu means alcohol. Ask before accepting a pour if you are avoiding strong liquor.
common_options: small glass | with food | share bottle | no alcohol
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly rượu đế.
quick_say_english: I’d like one glass of Vietnamese rice liquor.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht lee roo-uh day
what_it_is: Rượu đế is a traditional strong rice spirit, often served with food in small pours.
how_to_enjoy: Sip carefully and eat with it. Strength can vary, especially with homemade or local bottles.
worth_knowing: This belongs to Vietnam’s rice-liquor culture, not the beer or soda lane.
traveler_caution: Alcoholic and can be strong.
